title.en: Industry: public sector, IPR 1956 and small-scale industry
title.kn: ಕೈಗಾರಿಕೆ: ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕ ವಲಯ, 1956ರ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕಾ ನೀತಿ ನಿರ್ಣಯ ಮತ್ತು ಸಣ್ಣ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕೆ

heading.en: Why did the state build steel plants?

hook.en: In the 1950s Indian industrialists did not have enough capital to build huge steel plants and dams. So who would build them?
hook.kn: 1950ರ ದಶಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾರತೀಯ ಉದ್ಯಮಿಗಳ ಬಳಿ ದೊಡ್ಡ ಉಕ್ಕಿನ ಕಾರ್ಖಾನೆ ಕಟ್ಟುವಷ್ಟು ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಇರಲಿಲ್ಲ. ಹಾಗಾದರೆ ಯಾರು ಕಟ್ಟಬೇಕು?

objectives.en: Explain the role of the public sector
Explain the role of small-scale industry

narration.en: In the 1950s Indian industrialists did not have enough capital to build huge steel plants and dams. So who would build them?
narration.kn: 1950ರ ದಶಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾರತೀಯ ಉದ್ಯಮಿಗಳ ಬಳಿ ದೊಡ್ಡ ಉಕ್ಕಿನ ಕಾರ್ಖಾನೆ ಕಟ್ಟುವಷ್ಟು ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಇರಲಿಲ್ಲ. ಹಾಗಾದರೆ ಯಾರು ಕಟ್ಟಬೇಕು?

body.en: The state took a leading role in industry because Indian industrialists lacked capital and the market was too small. The Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 classified industries into three categories: the first owned exclusively by the state, the second where the private sector could supplement the state, and the third left to the private sector. Private industry was controlled through licences.
body.kn: ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಕೊರತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸಣ್ಣ ಮಾರುಕಟ್ಟೆಯ ಕಾರಣ ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮುಂದಾಳತ್ವ ವಹಿಸಿತು. 1956ರ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕಾ ನೀತಿ ನಿರ್ಣಯ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕೆಗಳನ್ನು ಮೂರು ವರ್ಗಗಳಾಗಿ ವಿಂಗಡಿಸಿತು. ಖಾಸಗಿ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕೆಗೆ ಪರವಾನಗಿ ಕಡ್ಡಾಯವಾಯಿತು.

points.en: IPR 1956 formed the basis of the Second Five Year Plan
Licences were used to promote industry in backward regions
Licences were also needed to expand output

narration.en: From 1951 to 1990 industry, led by the public sector under the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956, grew at about 6% a year. Growth compounds: the index (1951 = 100) multiplies by the same factor each year. At 6% a year, about how many years does output take to double? Compare 6% with 3.5% over forty years. How big is the gap by 1991?
narration.kn: 1951ರಿಂದ 1990ರವರೆಗೆ 1956ರ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕಾ ನೀತಿ ನಿರ್ಣಯದಡಿ ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕ ವಲಯದ ನೇತೃತ್ವದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕೆ ವರ್ಷಕ್ಕೆ ಸುಮಾರು 6% ಬೆಳೆಯಿತು. ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ ಚಕ್ರಬಡ್ಡಿಯಂತೆ: ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ (1951 = 100) ಪ್ರತಿ ವರ್ಷ ಒಂದೇ ಅಂಶದಿಂದ ಗುಣಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ವರ್ಷಕ್ಕೆ 6% ಆದರೆ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ ದ್ವಿಗುಣಕ್ಕೆ ಸುಮಾರು ಎಷ್ಟು ವರ್ಷ? 40 ವರ್ಷಗಳಲ್ಲಿ 6% ಮತ್ತು 3.5% ಹೋಲಿಸಿ. 1991ರಲ್ಲಿ ಅಂತರ ಎಷ್ಟು?

title.en: On the board: IPR 1956 and small industry

say.en: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 put industries in three categories.
First: state only, like atomic energy. Second: state leads, private supplements. Third: private.
Private firms needed a licence to start or expand: this was the licence system.
The Karve Committee of 1955 backed small industries. In 1950 the investment limit was 5 lakh rupees.

prompt.en: Sort each industry into its category under the IPR 1956.
prompt.kn: IPR 1956 ರ ಅಡಿ ಪ್ರತಿ ಉದ್ಯಮವನ್ನು ಅದರ ವರ್ಗಕ್ಕೆ ವಿಂಗಡಿಸಿ.

label.en: 2nd: state leads, private may join (Schedule B)

explanation.en: The first category was owned exclusively by the state; in the second the state would set up new units with private help; the rest was left to the private sector, controlled through licences.

body.en: In 1955 the Village and Small-Scale Industries Committee, also called the Karve Committee, noted that small industries could promote rural development. Small-scale industry is defined by the maximum investment allowed in its assets; in 1950 the limit was ₹5 lakh. SSIs are labour-intensive, so they generate more employment, and some goods were reserved for them.
body.kn: 1955ರ ಗ್ರಾಮ ಮತ್ತು ಸಣ್ಣ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕಾ ಸಮಿತಿ (ಕರ್ವೆ ಸಮಿತಿ) ಸಣ್ಣ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕೆಗಳು ಗ್ರಾಮೀಣಾಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿಗೆ ಸಹಾಯಕ ಎಂದಿತು. ಸಣ್ಣ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕೆಯನ್ನು ಆಸ್ತಿಗಳ ಮೇಲಿನ ಗರಿಷ್ಠ ಹೂಡಿಕೆಯಿಂದ ವ್ಯಾಖ್ಯಾನಿಸಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ; 1950ರಲ್ಲಿ ಮಿತಿ ₹5 ಲಕ್ಷ.

problem.en: Classify these under IPR 1956: (a) atomic energy, (b) a fertiliser plant where private firms could also invest alongside the state, (c) a biscuit factory.

steps.en: (a) Atomic energy: first category, exclusively owned by the state.
(b) Fertiliser plant: second category, private sector supplements the state.
(c) Biscuit factory: third category, left to the private sector (with licensing).
